subject: Re: EU hosting, VPC deployment controls and attestation
content:
--- Message 1 (oldest) ---
From: Maya Singh <security@acme-corp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-08T09:14:00Z
Subject: Data residency and VPC controls for EU deployment

Hi Soojin,

We're kicking off our SIG/CAIQ review for the upcoming PoC and need to confirm a few things before we proceed: 1) Will Acme customer data for the PoC be stored and processed only in EU-hosted regions (no US/APAC egress)? 2) For Redwood Private / VPC deployments: can you confirm the control plane topology, whether the control plane is customer-managed in VPC deployments, and whether KMS/HSM integrations are supported (we require customer-managed keys)? 3) Do you have an attestation or signed statement we can attach to our vendor risk record that states region residency guarantees for a named account?

Please attach any relevant architecture diagrams and a short timeline for getting a signed attestation. We're trying to close the SIG in two weeks.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Security Manager, Acme Corp
acme-security-team@acme-corp.com

--- Message 2 ---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-09T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency and VPC controls for EU deployment

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list.  Below is a concise summary and the attachments you requested; happy to expand any section.

1) Region residency
- For Hosted accounts, customers can select an EU region during provisioning. Current EU regions offered for production: eu-west-1 (Ireland), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt).
- For Dedicated and Private (VPC) deployments we can guarantee data-at-rest and processing within the selected EU region(s) for a given account ID once the account is provisioned and pinned to that region; we do not replicate primary customer data outside the chosen region unless explicitly configured for cross-region disaster recovery.

2) VPC / Private deployment controls
- Private deployment options: (a) VPC peered Private (control plane hosted by Redwood but logically isolated per customer and bound to customer VPC), or (b) Fully private / on-prem where control plane components can be customer-hosted.
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM: supported for Private deployments (bring-your-own-key). We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSMs via KMIP for on-prem.
- Audit logs: request/response tracing, token-level usage logs, and model-inference audit trails are retained per the contract; default retention 90 days for Hosted, configurable for Private/Dedicated.

3) Artifacts and evidence
- Attached: redwood-eu-arch-diagram.pdf (high-level architecture), vpc-deployment-guide.pdf (deployment checklist), SOC2-type2-summary.pdf (what we can share publicly).
- We can provide a short signed attestation that states: "For acct <AcmeAcct-0001>, Redwood Inference will store and process customer data only within EU regions (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1) and will not transfer primary customer data to other regions without prior written consent." This will be provided on Redwood letterhead and can be routed through DocuSign.

Next steps:
- Tell me the exact account identifier you will use for the PoC (so we can pin residency).
- Confirm if you need the Bring-Your-Own-Key integration and which provider (AWS/Azure/HSM).
- If you approve the attestation text above, I will loop in Legal and Rishi to finalize and send DocuSign.

Regards,
So: Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-eu-arch-diagram.pdf (diagram stub), vpc-deployment-guide.pdf (doc stub), SOC2-type2-summary.pdf (summary stub)

--- Message 3 ---
From: Maya Singh <security@acme-corp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-09T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency and VPC controls for EU deployment

Thanks Soojin — that reads well. A couple of clarifications before we ask procurement to onboard the attestation:
- We need the attestation to explicitly name the Acme account (AcmeAcct-0001) and include the phrase "will store and process customer data only within EU regions (eu-west-1 and/or eu-central-1)".
- Include a sentence confirming that control plane metrics/management metadata will not contain raw customer payloads and that telemetry needed for operations is pseudonymized.
- Can you share a target date when we can expect a signed DocuSign envelope? Two weeks would be tight but helpful.

If you prefer, send over a draft attestation and we'll circulate internally.

Best,
Maya

--- Message 4 ---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Singh <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T08:33:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Draft attestation for Acme (need signoff)

Rishi / Laura — forwarding Acme's request.  They want a short signed attestation naming acct AcmeAcct-0001 and confirming EU-only residency and a line about control plane telemetry pseudonymization.  Below is the draft attestation text I propose. Can you please review and confirm we can sign as-is or suggest edits? Acme is on a tight SIG timeline.

--- Proposed attestation (draft) ---
Redwood Inference Attestation
Date: [to be completed]

For the account AcmeAcct-0001, Redwood Inference confirms that primary customer data (including inputs to the model and generated outputs) will be stored and processed only within EU-hosted regions (eu-west-1 and/or eu-central-1) for the duration of the PoC and ongoing service unless otherwise agreed in writing. Redwood will not transfer, replicate, or process primary customer data in regions outside the EU without the customer’s prior written consent.

Control plane telemetry and operational metadata required for monitoring and service health do not contain raw customer payloads. Where operational telemetry could contain sensitive identifiers, Redwood pseudonymizes or redacts such fields according to our internal data handling policies.

Signed,
Redwood Inference (Authorized Signatory)

--- End draft ---

Can we: 1) approve this wording; 2) confirm whether Legal needs to add the SOC2 reference line; and 3) confirm which signer (Legal or Sales Ops) will be on the DocuSign?

Thanks,
So

--- Message 5 (latest) ---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Maya Singh <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T11:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft attestation for Acme (need signoff)

LGTM with two small edits: 1) change "primary customer data (including inputs to the model and generated outputs)" to "primary customer data (including customer inputs to the model and corresponding outputs)" for clarity; 2) add a final sentence: "A redacted SOC 2 Type II report summary is available to Acme upon execution of a standard NDA."

I'll ask Legal to attach the SOC2 summary after NDA and I'll be the DocuSign signer for this attestation.

Once I have the Legal note I'll route the envelope; target to get this signed within 3 business days.

Thanks — Rishi

--- End of thread ---
